key_insight: Hidden-parameter coverage and antipodal separation govern shallow ReLU^k networks’ approximation accuracy, spectral conditioning, and coefficient stability on bounded domains.
engineering_relevance: Parameter geometry offers a principled guide for selecting network features and assessing stability in function approximation and discrete least-squares recovery.
method: Quantify parameter geometry using fill distance h and antipodal separation.
Use smooth localization and dyadic Fourier estimates to derive approximation and saturation bounds.
Analyze Gram and stiffness spectra, norm discretization, and regularized recovery.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds rather than empirical benchmarks, including an interior approximation rate h^r up to critical regularity (d+2k+1)/2 and an asymptotic lower bound for smoother fixed targets.
watch_item: Upper and lower approximation bounds concern different spatial domains, so they should not be interpreted as directly matching global error estimates.
paper_title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation and Stability Properties of Shallow ReLU$^k$ Networks on Bounded Euclidean Domains
